items.title: Dave Williams Interview, 1961-07-02
items.q: You're leading that band? That's my band, yeah. Uh-huh. And you've got Sam Dutre in there?

ctx.x: I'll make a note on the tape here that we're interviewing Mr. Dave Williams at his home, 1901 Milton, isn't it? Up near St. Bernard and the date is July the 2nd, 1961. So, when we go to transcribe this in there, look at what tape it is.

Now, this band you're playing at Leroy's on Burmese Street with, Dave, is that your band? You're leading that band? That's my band, yeah. Uh-huh. And you've got Sam Dutre in there? And who else is in the band with you?
Willie Joss, Josh Willis at least. You know Josh Willis the trumpet man? Uh-huh. And Marvin, Tram Martin, Justin Joss on the drum. And then McNeil Groh was on the bass.

items.title: Dave Williams Interview, 1974-03-28
items.q: I have Kimball, the big clarinet player that died there. Sam Dutre. And all those boys working with me.

ctx.x: Yeah. You know, when I went in there sometime, Willie Humphrey would be there with you. Do you remember that?

Well, I'm happy to play some chimes, which I mean he wouldn't ever mention that he played with such a small musician like me, you know. Many of them wouldn't. Yeah, but I was there. I remember. Yeah, but I know you know. Just like, you remember when I was working for Leroy, the first patio out in there on Boyfriend Street? Mm-hmm. And I had Frog, Tramore Man, Frog. I had Jack Willis. I have Kimball, the big clarinet player that died there. Sam Dutre. And all those boys working with me. But right now, they…
Are you any kin to George Williams? No, I'm not kin to George Williams. Did you ever know him?
